# How to use custom GPTs (and build your own without coding)

Imagine having a digital assistant who already knows your household budget, your business's brand voice, or your weekly fitness goals, without you having to explain it every single time you open a chat. This is the power of **custom GPTs** – personalized versions of ChatGPT built for a single, specific task. Building one needs no computer code; you simply have a conversation with the AI about what you need. Note, though, that new GPT creation is currently not available on personal ChatGPT accounts (see the update below).

This guide will show you how to find ready-made helpers in the GPT Store and how building your own tailored AI assistant works in the workspaces where it is still possible. While your custom GPT is great at conversation and information processing, it can't directly connect to external apps like your smart fridge or automatically order groceries for you.

> **Important update:** According to OpenAI, new GPT creation and publishing are not available on personal ChatGPT accounts, including Free, Go, Plus and Pro. Creation remains possible in some Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces, depending on workspace settings and permissions. OpenAI has also announced that it plans to retire custom GPTs and move creators to plugins; the standard retirement date is scheduled for December 11, 2026, and existing GPTs stay usable until then. Check the notice in your own account for the dates that apply to you.

## Before you start
- **A ChatGPT account:** You can browse and use GPTs with a free ChatGPT account. Creating a *new* GPT is not possible on personal accounts (Free, Go, Plus or Pro); it is only available in some Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces, when your workspace settings and permissions allow it.
- **A device:** You can browse and use GPTs from a web browser on a computer or through the ChatGPT app on a smartphone or tablet. Building a GPT is possible on the web only, not in the mobile apps.
- **An idea:** If you plan to build your own (where it's available to you), think of a repetitive task you do often, such as drafting weekly emails, planning school lunches, or organizing meeting notes.
- **Rough total time:** This guide should take about 6-10 minutes to follow, not including the time you might spend experimenting with your new GPT.

## Step 1 — Explore the GPT Store
First, you'll need to open ChatGPT. On a computer, go to chatgpt.com; on a smartphone, open the ChatGPT app. In the sidebar, look for **Explore GPTs** and open it (you can also go straight to chatgpt.com/gpts). If you can't see the sidebar, look for a menu button that opens it. The GPT Store is like a digital marketplace, but instead of apps, it's filled with helpful **chatbots** (computer programs designed to simulate human conversation) created by other people and companies.

You'll know it worked when: you see a directory of different custom GPTs that you can browse or search.

## Step 2 — Use a pre-made helper
Before building your own, let’s try using one! Once you're in the GPT Store, you can browse or search to find something specific. Open any GPT that catches your eye.

What happens next is the selected GPT's dedicated chat window will open, ready for you to interact with it. If it looks different, some GPTs might show an initial welcome message or suggested prompts, while others might just present a blank chat box. One thing to know: according to OpenAI, GPTs do not use your saved memory, custom instructions or previous conversations, so each conversation starts fresh.

💬 Example: Search for "Book recommendations". Open one of the results, then type: *"I loved 'Dune' by Frank Herbert. What should I read next that has a similar epic feel?"*

You'll know it worked when: you see a chat with the chosen GPT, and you can type your message and get an answer.

## Step 3 — Start building your own custom helper (where available)
Building is only possible if your account or workspace allows it. If your Business, Enterprise or Edu workspace lets you create GPTs, open **Explore GPTs** (or go to chatgpt.com/gpts) and select **Create** to open the GPT builder. In the builder you can either describe what you want in a conversation, or set up the GPT directly by editing its fields. There is also a built-in preview so you can test the GPT while you build it.

If it looks different: If you can't find a **Create** option, new GPT creation isn't available for your account or workspace. That is expected on personal ChatGPT accounts, including Plus.

You'll know it worked when: the GPT builder opens and you can start describing your helper.

## Step 4 — Tell the builder what you want
In the conversational builder, describe what you want in plain, everyday English, just as you would talk to a helpful colleague. You don't need technical jargon or code; simply describe your idea. For instance, if you're looking for a cooking assistant, you might describe its purpose directly.

What happens next is ChatGPT will help draft the GPT based on your description, filling in fields such as its name, description and instructions. You can accept these drafts or ask for changes. If it looks different, the builder might ask a clarifying question first, especially if your description was broad.

💬 Example: Type this into the builder:
> *"I want to build a helper that takes a messy list of ingredients from my fridge and suggests three simple dinner options, organized by preparation time."*

You'll know it worked when: the builder responds with a first draft of your GPT, for example a suggested name and description.

## Step 5 — Refine your helper's personality and rules
Next, adjust the **instructions**. Instructions define how your GPT behaves: what it should do, how it should respond, and what it should avoid. They are applied to every conversation and guide the GPT's tone and decisions. You can refine them through the builder conversation or by editing the instructions field directly. OpenAI recommends concrete, positive instructions ("Do X") over long lists of prohibitions.

What happens next is the GPT's instructions are updated based on your feedback. If it looks different, the exact layout of the editor may vary between workspaces and app versions.

💬 Example: You might tell the builder:
> *"The tone should be warm and encouraging. Never suggest recipes that require more than four pots and pans, and always assume the user has basic pantry items like salt, pepper, and olive oil."*

You'll know it worked when: your new rules show up in the GPT's instructions.

## Step 6 — Test your new GPT
Before saving your custom GPT, it's essential to test it to make sure it works exactly as you intended. Use the built-in **Preview** to try your GPT: type questions or scenarios just as a real user would, and check whether the responses fit your rules and desired tone.

What happens next is your custom GPT will respond based on the instructions you've given it. If it looks different, and the preview isn't responding or gives unexpected answers, go back to the instructions and refine them further.

💬 Example: In the preview, type: *"I have eggs, leftover roast pumpkin, and spinach."*

You'll know it worked when: your custom GPT provides suggestions that follow the rules you set, like suggesting simple dinner options without too many pots.

## Step 7 — Save and share your creation
Changes save to a draft automatically while you edit. When you're happy with how your GPT performs, select **Create** in an eligible workspace (if you're editing an existing GPT, it says **Update**). To see how you can share it, select **Share**: the options depend on your account and workspace settings, and in Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces they can include sharing with specific people, within the workspace, by link, or publishing to the GPT Store when permitted. Publishing new GPTs is not available on personal accounts.

To change a GPT later, open **Explore GPTs**, select **My GPTs**, choose the GPT and select **Edit GPT**.

You'll know it worked when: your GPT appears under **My GPTs** and can be opened by the people you shared it with.

## Common mistakes
- **Sharing private information:** Never put sensitive personal or confidential business data into the general instructions of your custom GPT. The AI might accidentally include it in a response to a user, or it could be stored in a way you didn't intend.
    *   **Fix:** Keep instructions general and focus on the *type* of information to process, not specific sensitive details. If you need to work with private data, use a custom GPT privately and manually input sensitive bits for single-use scenarios, deleting the chat history afterwards.
- **Overcomplicating the rules:** Trying to give the AI fifty rules at once can sometimes confuse it, leading it to ignore some instructions. It's like trying to tell too many people too many things at once.
    *   **Fix:** Start with one or two simple, clear rules. Test it, then add more details incrementally. You can always edit your custom GPT later to refine its instructions.
- **Not being specific enough:** While plain language is good, vague requests like "be helpful" can lead to generic or uninspired responses from your GPT.
    *   **Fix:** Think about *exactly* what "helpful" means for your task. Instead of "be helpful," try "be helpful by suggesting solutions and providing pros and cons for each." The more specific you are, the better the AI can tailor its responses.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can try ready-made GPTs for things like recipe ideas, study help or trip planning, instead of writing long instructions yourself every time.
- **For your business or work:** If your organization uses ChatGPT Business, Enterprise or Edu, ask your workspace admin whether GPT creation is still enabled for you, and how your team plans to move reusable workflows to plugins.
- **If you're just getting started:** You don't need to build anything right away. Simply browsing the GPT Store is a fantastic way to see how other people are using AI to make their daily tasks easier and spark ideas for your own needs.

## Try it now
Open ChatGPT, select **Explore GPTs** in your sidebar, and search for the word **"Recipe"**. Open a recipe suggestion helper and type in the names of three ingredients you currently have in your fridge to see what it suggests next. It takes less than two minutes and is a great introduction to how specialized these helpers can be.
